football_evidence.question: Can East Carolina win at the line of scrimmage?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward East Carolina, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 3.3 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When UAB has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): UAB’s offense has allowed a sack on 10.6% of its dropbacks, and East Carolina’s defense sacks the quarterback on 11.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When UAB has the ball (big plays on the ground): UAB’s offense turns 4.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and East Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.7% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When UAB has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): UAB’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 12.8% of its runs, and East Carolina’s defense stops 30.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When East Carolina has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): East Carolina’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 15.2% of its runs, and UAB’s defense stops 10.4% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).
contradicting: When East Carolina has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): East Carolina’s offense has allowed a sack on 6.9% of its dropbacks, and UAB’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.0% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When East Carolina has the ball (third down): East Carolina’s offense converts 23.5% of its third downs, and UAB’s defense allows opponents to convert 36.6% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When East Carolina has the ball (big plays through the air): East Carolina’s offense turns 8.7% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and UAB’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.0% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).
